{"id": "2:204/q24", "question": "What does the verse teach about disputation?", "turns_on": "Whether the blame falls on all dispute or on dishonest and excessive quarrelling.", "positions": [{"id": "2:204/q24/p1", "position": "False, crooked, excessive or abusive dispute is sinful and marks hypocrisy.", "reasons": "TUSTARI:2:204/r2 (TUSTARI; reports): Aisha reports Prophet: most hateful men to God is fiercely contentious adversary. BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r1 (النبي; reports): Aisha reports the Prophet saying that the most hateful men to God are the fiercely contentious disputants; the author gives no grading. QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r13 (author; holds): The description shows that disputation is permissible only when what is outwardly said agrees with what is inwardly true. QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#3/r1 (النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم; reports): Aisha reports the Prophet saying that the most hateful of men to God is the obstinate, contentious adversary. IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563#2/r2 (رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم; reports): A sound Prophetic report gives lying when speaking, betrayal when pledged, and wickedness in dispute as three signs of a hypocrite. DURR-FULL:v1p573/r10 (ابن شبرمة; reports): Ibn Shubrumah says excessive quarrelling is sinful; he also transmits maxims linking poor restraint in dispute with inability to bear truth and praising patience and chastity. DURR-FULL:v1p573/r4 (عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم; reports): ʿAʾisha reports the Prophet saying that the most hateful men to God are the contentious adversaries. DURR-FULL:v1p573/r5 (عبد الله بن عمرو عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم; reports): The Prophet lists four traits of a complete hypocrite: betraying trust, lying, breaking a pact, and speaking abusively in an argument; any one is a trait of hypocrisy until abandoned. DURR-FULL:v1p573/r6 (ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم; reports): Ibn ʿAbbas reports the Prophet saying that continual disputation is sufficient to make a person sinful. DURR-FULL:v1p573/r7 (أبو الدرداء; reports): Abu al-Dardaʾ says continual disputation suffices for sin, continual hostility for injustice, and continual talk about God for lying. DURR-FULL:v1p573/r8 (أبو الدرداء; reports): Abu al-Dardaʾ says much speech brings much lying, frequent oaths bring much sin, and frequent quarrels endanger one’s religion. DURR-FULL:v1p573/r9 (عبد الكريم الجزري; reports): ʿAbd al-Karim al-Jazari says that no scrupulously pious person has ever quarreled. ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r15 (author; holds): The verse signals that excessive quarrelsomeness is blameworthy and characteristic of hypocrites, who love worldly life and therefore dispute over it.
